at-0Ecv.title: Chevron: white on red or red on yellow
at-0Ecv.summary: Two colour styles: white on red, or red on yellow. Germany mostly uses red on white and only rarely red on yellow.

differs.how: Germany mostly uses red on white

at-0jT0.title: Google car: tin foil antenna
at-0jT0.summary: A tin-foil-looking antenna, mostly in western Austria near the Swiss border. Unique here.

at-3bP3.title: Buses: each state has its own bus company
at-3bP3.summary: Each state has its own bus company, with its logo on the side of buses.

at-3ouy.title: Landscape: forested mountains, flatter east
at-3ouy.summary: Most of the country is mountainous and forested, but parts of the east and northeast are flatter and agricultural.

at-6K4Z.title: Pole: yellow and white stripes
at-6K4Z.summary: Yellow-and-white stripes around poles and signposts are found in Vorarlberg, the far west.

at-9j96.title: Route marker: A-road numbers rise westward
at-9j96.summary: Motorway numbers get bigger the further west you go.

at-AH8p.title: Pole: red-and-white tape like the flag
at-AH8p.summary: Red-and-white tape resembling the national flag appears on poles in Vienna and Innsbruck. In Vienna the tape is thinner and there are usually two on each pole.

at-Aj8O.title: Sign: No Stopping with Anfang or Ende
at-Aj8O.summary: No Stopping and No Waiting signs often have Anfang (beginning) or Ende (end) written on or below them.

at-FhCj.title: Sign: white Güterweg, black outline
at-FhCj.summary: White Güterweg signs with a black outline are mainly found in Upper Austria.

at-KsHC.title: Sign: mounted with four metal clips
at-KsHC.summary: Road signs are sometimes held by four metal clips, which is unique in central Europe. Many are fixed other ways, though.

at-Lxtx.title: Sign: dead end with white upside-down T
at-Lxtx.summary: Simple dead-end signs with a white upside-down T are mostly unique. Most of Europe uses a different design, and older Swiss coverage used this one too.

differs.how: Older Swiss coverage used the same sign

at-N5fI.title: Coverage: Gen 3 and Gen 4 only, never low-cam
at-N5fI.summary: Austria has mainly the older Gen 3 and the newer Gen 4. Germany has only Gen 4, and Switzerland is always low-cam with a much bigger car blur.

differs.how: Switzerland always has the big car blur of a low camera

at-NQvW.title: Plate: long white, one blue strip
at-NQvW.summary: Long white plates with the blue EU strip on the left only. Italian plates have two blue strips and are shorter; Swiss plates are long and white but have no blue strip.

differs.how: Italian plates are shorter with a blue strip on both sides
Swiss plates have no blue strip

at-PGTR.title: Language: German letters Ä Ö Ü ß
at-PGTR.summary: German uses the special letters Ä, Ö, Ü and ß. Germany and Switzerland are also German-speaking, as are East Belgium and South Tyrol in Italy.

at-UnOK.title: Road: large white painted square
at-UnOK.summary: A big white painted square in the middle of the road next to kilometre markers means Salzburg state.

at-W0XX.title: Direction sign: white, blue outline, special font
at-W0XX.summary: Direction signs are white with a blue outline and a distinctive font.

at-Wz4z.title: Kilometre marker: white
at-Wz4z.summary: White kilometre markers are in Vorarlberg and on one road in western Salzburg.

at-XNJA.title: Pole: round wooden
at-XNJA.summary: Round wooden poles are the most common utility poles.

at-Z6SF.title: Bollard: white, black top, dark red reflector
at-Z6SF.summary: White post with a black top and a dark red or dark grey reflector. Many have a small black nipple-shaped cap, and some have a snow pole on top. Slovenia and Montenegro use similar ones with a bright red reflector.

differs.how: German posts are plain white with grey reflectors

at-auEK.title: Street sign: dark blue, white serif, district no.
at-auEK.summary: The capital's street signs are dark blue plaques with a traditional white serif font. The number at the start is the district.

at-aurF.title: Pedestrian sign: two dashed lines, no stripes
at-aurF.summary: Pedestrian signs show two horizontal dashed lines instead of zebra stripes. All neighbouring countries use zebra stripes.

at-brez.title: Flags: each state has its own flag
at-brez.summary: Every state has its own flag, which you may see on buildings.

at-byhm.title: Sign: yellow and blue borders
at-byhm.summary: In Lower Austria, signs may have yellow and blue borders matching the regional flag.

at-ctpi.title: Landscape: tallest sharp Alps
at-ctpi.summary: The highest Alps are in the west and centre. The tallest mountains are in the narrow southern strip on the Italian border, with sharper peaks and a grander look.

at-jkM9.title: Sign: green local-facility signs
at-jkM9.summary: Green signs are common, pointing to local facilities.

at-jtGs.title: Google car: low camera, big round blur
at-jtGs.summary: A low-mounted Gen 4 camera with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through, which makes it easy to miss. Most of Western Europe has it too.

at-lm-295899.title: Street sign: red
at-lm-295899.summary: Dornbirn, in the far west, has red street signs.

at-lm-295900.title: Street sign: green with two lines
at-lm-295900.summary: Graz has green street signs with two lines of text.

at-lm-295901.title: Street sign: large, heading plus small text
at-lm-295901.summary: Innsbruck has large street signs with a heading and small text underneath.

at-lm-295903.title: Buses: Landbus logo
at-lm-295903.summary: The public transport company in Vorarlberg, in the far west, is called Landbus. Its logo is on buses there.

at-lm-295904.title: Buses: OÖVV logo
at-lm-295904.summary: The public transport company in Upper Austria is called OÖVV, and its logo is on buses there.

at-lm-295905.title: Buses: Wiener Linien logo
at-lm-295905.summary: The capital's transport company is Wiener Linien. Its logo is on buses and trams in and around the city.

at-lm-295906.title: Buses: Graz Holding logo
at-lm-295906.summary: The transport company in Graz is called Graz Holding, with its logo on buses and trams.

at-lm-295907.title: Buses: RegioBus Steiermark logo
at-lm-295907.summary: Styria's transport company is RegioBus Steiermark, with its logo on buses there.

at-lm-295912.title: Street sign: blue or white with coat of arms
at-lm-295912.summary: Linz has blue signs with a distinctive font, and white signs with a red frame and a coat of arms.

at-lm-361745.title: Phone numbers: area code 01 up to 07
at-lm-361745.summary: Area codes run from 01 for the capital up to 07.

at-lm-634057.title: Plate: thin red edge around blue strip
at-lm-634057.summary: Long white plate with the blue EU strip plus a tiny bit of red around it and on the left, often hard to see. This is how to tell it from Germany, which has just the plain EU plate.

differs.how: German plates have only the plain blue EU strip

at-lm-740318.hide: no learnable content (image-only street sign note)

at-lm-740320.title: Street sign: white, orange stripes and logo
at-lm-740320.summary: Linz also has black signs with white text, and a unique white one with orange stripes above and below and an orange logo on the left.

at-lm-740321.hide: no learnable content (image-only street sign note)

at-lm-740534.title: Street sign: very dark red-brown, white text
at-lm-740534.summary: Innsbruck has very dark red or brown street signs with white text.

at-mNtb.title: Bus stop: neon-yellow poles
at-mNtb.summary: Bus stops made of neon-yellow poles are in Vorarlberg, the far west.

at-nkbT.title: Sign: bus stop with yellow-green circle and H
at-nkbT.summary: Bus stop signs show a yellow and green circle with the letter H. Germany is the only other country with similar signs.

at-pHCf.title: Landscape: huge lake in the far west
at-pHCf.summary: Lake Constance (Bodensee) on the western border is recognisable by its vast size, unlike other lakes in the mountains.

at-pdDS.title: Route marker: B-roads rise westward
at-pdDS.summary: B-roads, white text in a blue rectangle, also rise in number from east to west. The exception is 222 to 230, around the capital.

at-qDvc.title: Pole: yellow gas marker, like a snow pole
at-qDvc.summary: Yellow natural gas poles that look like snow poles. Unique here.

at-scuj.title: Plants: vineyards in the far east
at-scuj.summary: Vineyards are limited to the far east, with many near Vienna and around Lake Neusiedl.

at-wOk9.title: Landscape: height shows the region
at-wOk9.summary: Height is key. The centre and west are the most mountainous; flatter parts are in the east near the borders, though even those have rolling hills.

at-whoL.title: Street sign: each big city has its own
at-whoL.summary: Many cities have their own street signs. The blue ones look alike, but can be told apart: Vienna by district number, Salzburg by its font, Klagenfurt by an irregular white border, St Pölten by a rounded white border.

at-wkwt.title: Sign: one-way sign says EINBAHN
at-wkwt.summary: One-way signs with the word EINBAHN are unique. German ones say Einbahnstraße.

at-xfLD.title: Sign: white town sign, blue outline
at-xfLD.summary: Similar white signs with a blue outline and the same font mark the entrance of towns. Germany uses yellow town signs with a black outline.

differs.how: German town signs are yellow with a black outline

at-yHR2.title: Sign: green Güterweg sign
at-yHR2.summary: Green Güterweg (local farm road) signs are found in Burgenland, in the east.

at-zEpW.title: Route marker: blue with white number and comma
at-zEpW.summary: Blue markers with white numbers that have one decimal after a comma. Slovenian markers are white, and German ones have a thin white outline.

differs.how: German markers have a thin white outline

at-zryZ.title: Houses: light walls, wooden balconies, wide roofs
at-zryZ.summary: Alpine houses with light walls, wooden balconies or panelling on the top floor, and dark wooden roofs that stick out. Often several floors. Southern Germany builds in a similar way.
